supersedes: generator-skill-effect-v1 (INCONCLUSIVE: no-skill baseline 0.927 above the 0.90 ceiling)
hypothesis: On tasks where a tool-enabled claude-sonnet-5-5 without the skill leaves seeded faults undetected, following the playwright-test-generator skill (full workflow) raises the effective fault-kill rate of the delivered Playwright specs without lowering the rate at which they pass on the correct application. Secondary questions: whether a lean variant that keeps the skill's scenario, locator, assertion, run-and-fix and scanner rules but drops its exploration, approval, tracer, V1-V6 and independent-reviewer layers (a) also beats no-skill and (b) is non-inferior to the full skill at a fraction of its cost; and whether either variant raises survival of a behavior-preserving markup refactor.
design_notes: Same staging and deterministic scoring as v1 (fresh project per call, Git baseline, Playwright 1.62 webServer on a loopback port; scoring = 3 clean runs, one run per seeded fault variant, one run on the markup refactor, scanner smell counts; no model judge). Three changes: (1) a pool of new tasks written as user briefs rather than numbered checklists, on apps with multi-step flows, server persistence, ordering and error-recovery behavior, each fault tied to a quoted phrase of the brief (validated); (2) a headroom screen that runs only the no-skill arm on the whole pool and keeps the tasks whose mean no-skill primary lies in a pre-stated band, frozen before any skill-arm call; (3) a final comparison on the kept tasks with fresh repetitions and a different seed, plus deterministic process-compliance indicators parsed from the stream-json transcript. Nothing the model sees names a fault, a fault class, the screen, or this benchmark.

arms.full: same prompt, tools, approvals and project, plus an instruction to read and follow the working-tree playwright-test-generator skill (SKILL.md and its reference files), staged outside the project with the working-tree e2e-reviewer skill its Step 6 invokes (Skill tool unavailable; the skill's inline fallback applies)
arms.lean: same prompt, tools, approvals and project, plus an instruction to read and follow benchmarks/generator-skill-effect-v2/arms/lean/SKILL.md, a benchmark-only text derived from the real skill by removing layers (never by adding advice), staged outside the project with the working-tree e2e-reviewer skill so its scan.sh step can run
arms.no-skill: same prompt, tools, approvals and project; no skill files staged

host.second_model_family: not run; single-host limit as in v1

load_pause: before each model call the runner waits (up to 30 minutes, in 60 s steps) while the 1-minute load average exceeds 12, and records the pause

screen.rule: Run only the no-skill arm, two repetitions per pool task, shuffled with the screen seed; neither full nor lean ever runs on the screening pool. Keep every task whose mean no-skill primary is in [0.40, 0.80]. If fewer than 12 tasks qualify, add tasks nearest to the band edges first, excluding any task whose mean is 0 or at/above 0.90, until 12 are kept, and list them as fallback_used_for. Freeze the kept set, the screen report digests and the spend before any full- or lean-arm call. Screening repetitions are never reused as final-comparison data.
screen.selection_effect: Selecting tasks on which the no-skill arm scored low makes its fresh final repetitions regress upward toward the pool mean; this works against finding a lift and may push the kept-set baseline back over the ceiling. The kept set is also enriched for tasks with ambiguous or flaky behavior. Both effects are reported, not corrected.

final.rule: Kept tasks only, all three arms, three fresh repetitions each, shuffled with the final seed, two workers. With 12 kept tasks this is 108 calls; v1 per-call costs (full $0.34, no-skill $0.06; lean expected between) put the stage near $20, far under the cap, so repetitions are not reduced.

agent_outcomes: a call that hits its wall-clock limit or per-call budget is scored on whatever spec files exist in tests/ at that moment and counted in the arm's timeout metric; only a CLI crash or a missing stream-json result event is retried, once, in a fresh staged project
deliverable: every new or modified file under tests/ at the end of the call (git status against the baseline commit); spec files among them (*.spec.* or *.test.*) are scored; writes outside tests/ are recorded and discarded (scoring uses the original app.mjs and config)

scoring.clean: spec files pass on the correct app in 3 of 3 separate runs
scoring.fault_kill: a fault variant is killed when at least one test fails on it with no Playwright-level error
scoring.refactor_score: 1 when the deliverable is clean and passes the behavior-preserving markup refactor (ids, classes, nesting renamed; roles, labels, names, text unchanged), else 0
scoring.smells: skills/e2e-reviewer/scripts/scan.sh on the delivered test files; P0 and P1/P2-heuristic counts (LLM-triage hits reported separately)
scoring.process_compliance: from tool_use blocks in the stream-json transcript: full SKILL.md read, lean SKILL.md read, e2e-reviewer SKILL.md read, app source read, `playwright test` runs, `--repeat-each` runs, scan.sh runs, browser-exploration commands (playwright cli / playwright-cli / agent-browser), git status calls, Agent spawns, writes outside tests/; counts only, no judgement; recorded for all three arms
scoring.cost: total_cost_usd, num_turns, usage, wall time from the result event

primary_metric: effective fault-kill rate per call (faults killed / 5, counted 0 unless clean); the overall verdict is decided by full versus no-skill on this metric alone
secondary_preregistered: lean versus no-skill on the primary metric, same rule as the primary comparison, reported as its own PASS/FAIL

lean non-inferiority to full: lean's mean primary and mean refactor score each no more than 0.10 below full's, the paired bootstrap 95% CI lower bound of lean minus full on the primary above -0.10, and lean's clean-pass rate not more than 0.05 below full's; cost and time multiples reported plainly
refactor survival score per call for full versus no-skill and lean versus no-skill, each with its own paired lift, CI and PASS/FAIL under decision_rule.secondary_refactor

primary.ci: paired case-cluster bootstrap of per-case mean differences (skill minus no-skill) over the kept tasks
primary.PASS: full minus no-skill lift >= 0.10 AND bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND full clean-pass rate >= no-skill clean-pass rate - 0.05 AND no-skill primary on the kept set < 0.90
primary.FAIL: every scheduled final call scored, no drift, no spend-cap stop, kept-set baseline below the ceiling, and PASS not met
primary.INCONCLUSIVE: any unscored call, drift, spend-cap stop, incomplete schedule, or a kept-set no-skill primary at or above the ceiling

secondary_refactor.PASS: lift >= 0.10 AND bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND no-skill refactor score < 0.90

lean_non_inferiority.PASS: lean mean primary >= full mean primary - 0.10 AND bootstrap 95% CI lower bound of (lean - full) on the primary > -0.10 AND lean mean refactor score >= full mean refactor score - 0.10 AND lean clean-pass rate >= full clean-pass rate - 0.05
lean_non_inferiority.FAIL: otherwise, with every final call scored
lean_non_inferiority.INCONCLUSIVE: any unscored call, drift, spend-cap stop or incomplete schedule

fault_classes.persistence: the page shows success but the server did not store or drop the change; only a reload or API read fails
fault_classes.ordering: fast or overlapping actions produce a stale or out-of-order result
fault_classes.recovery: after a failure the stated recovery (kept input, retry, restored state) does not happen
fault_classes.precision: a stated detail is wrong (exact text, count, order, absence, which item changed)
fault_classes.interaction: a stated keyboard, focus, enabled/disabled, dialog or clear-after-success behavior is missing
fault_classes.a11y: an accessible name or role the brief relies on regresses while the visible text stays
fault_classes.boundary: a stated limit is off by one or an edge state is wrong

fairness_rule: every fault carries a brief_phrase that must appear verbatim (case-insensitive) in the task text, so each fault breaks a behavior the brief states; validate enforces it
validation_rule: before the pool freeze, every pool task must pass validate: existing spec green under every fault, strong spec green twice, kills 5/5 and survives the refactor, naive spec misses >= 2 faults (a sanity floor, not a headroom claim; headroom is measured by the screen). The freeze refuses when validation reports any problem or when inputs changed after it.
power: No pilot variance for this metric on screened tasks. With 12 kept tasks and an assumed paired-difference SD of 0.30, each paired comparison has a standard error near 0.087 and a minimum detectable lift near 0.24 at 80% power (two-sided 0.05); the non-inferiority margin of 0.10 is therefore well inside the noise, so a non-inferiority PASS means 'no large deficit shown', not 'equivalent'. A true lift of 0.10 would usually go undetected.
contamination: the pool tasks were written for this protocol and are spent after it; v1's ten tasks and smoke task are not reused
limits: One host and model family; author-written apps; three final repetitions.
The screen selects tasks where one model's no-skill arm happened to score low: regression to the mean, flaky or ambiguous tasks, and the single-model selection all limit generalization.

The skill is built for an interactive approval gate; the harness pre-grants approvals in the shared prompt, so headless skill behavior (skipped exploration, probes or scanner) is part of what is measured and is reported through the compliance indicators.
A null result on the screened tasks does not show the skill is useless: it shows no measurable lift of this size on tasks this baseline already finds hard.
The lean arm is a benchmark-only text, not a shipped skill; a result for it says what the removed layers did or did not add under this harness, not that the real skill should be changed.

lean_arm.added: before the pool freeze and before any screening or final call, at the user's request, after v1 showed the full skill arm ending PARTIAL/BLOCKED in 27/30 calls (V2/V3 probes skipped, V6 separate-reviewer gate unmet, exploration replaced by source reading) at 6.05x the cost with no measured fault-kill benefit
lean_arm.derivation: Each sentence of arms/lean/SKILL.md traces to SKILL.md, best-practices.md, code-rules.md or scenario-design.md of the real skill (scenario admission minimum, the three secondary outcomes with the failed-write re-read rule, selector priority, hard rules, the forbidden-pattern table, independence rules, the repair boundary from verification-rules § Failure handling, and the Step 6 scanner gate). No rule was added that the real skill does not state.
kept: project profile (Step 1 Environment Detection, reduced to what the local project exposes)
scenario listing with one primary outcome per scenario, happy path plus error/edge minimum, error-cause signal (scenario-design.md)
the three default secondary outcomes (survives a reload, side effect proved, error cause distinguished) and the absence-after-failed-write re-read rule
selector priority, chain/filter over .nth(), no XPath or styling CSS (code-rules.md, best-practices.md § Locators)
await-everything, web-first assertions, one hard expect, the forbidden-pattern table (code-rules.md § Hard rules, § Spec Rules)
per-test independence and reset-in-beforeEach (code-rules.md § Spec Rules)
a run-and-fix loop bounded at three attempts that may change mechanics only and never weakens assertions (verification-rules.md § Failure handling, V6 repair boundary)
one scan.sh pass with P0/P1 fixes (SKILL.md Step 6, reduced from the full e2e-reviewer Phase 1-2 procedure to the mechanical scanner)
removed: Step 3 live browser exploration chain and its guards (Playwright CLI allowlist, preflight launcher, DNS snapshot, raw-ARIA fallback) and the starting write-set snapshot
Step 4 approval ceremony: scenario plan presentation, generated-file table, control-file table, target-controlled command table with effect labels, per-row approval
scenario admission bookkeeping (distinct risk, right layer, diagnostic handle, owner/source, confidence) and the Locator Mapping Table

V1-V6 verification ladder beyond the actual test run: V2 assertion falsification, V3 fault injection, V4 write-contract request proof, V5 replay-safety boundary (the --repeat-each run is kept), V6 independent fresh-context re-review and the completion status matrix
Step 6 full e2e-reviewer Phase 2 LLM review and the inline-fallback procedure (only the mechanical scanner is kept)
Step 5b conventions and seed artifacts, YAGNI audit, Page Object fallback template, network determinism, SSR/hydration, auth/session and branch-seeding sections
the safety preamble about untrusted page content and remote targets (the benchmark projects are local, trusted and disposable by construction)
Playwright Test Agents interop and imported-test-case handling
lean_arm.why: The removed layers are the ones v1's self-reports show being skipped, marked CANNOT_VERIFY, or substituted in headless use, and the ones that consume most of the skill's tokens; the kept layers are the ones that plausibly change what the test asserts (secondary outcomes, failed-write re-read) and how it locates elements (role/label/text), which are the behaviors the primary and secondary metrics measure.

arm_snapshots.source: working tree of the main checkout at commit 0c37f08 (release 2.0.0 plus the user's uncommitted e2e-reviewer edits: SKILL.md, scripts/scan.sh, references/grep-patterns.md, pattern-reference.md, patterns/10.md, 11.md, 19.md, 20.md, scanner-workflow.md, semantic-review.md, and the untracked scripts/pom-ownership-candidates.py); skills/playwright-test-generator had no uncommitted edits, so arms/full is byte-identical to the released 2.0.0 skill
arm_snapshots.shared: arms/shared/e2e-reviewer = skills/e2e-reviewer without evals/ (used by the full arm's Step 6 inline fallback, by the lean arm's scan step, and by the scorer's smell counts)
arm_snapshots.lean: arms/lean = the benchmark-only reduced text and its derivation trace
arm_snapshots.why: the repository skill is scheduled to change after this freeze (fixes folded into 2.0.0 without a version bump); all three arms and the scorer read only these snapshots, never skills/, so the measured bytes stay reproducible.
